spec_features.feature_name: least exposure / extract signal with least aversive exposure
spec_features.spec_quote: the experiment should extract the needed signal with the *least* exposure of the subject to a potentially aversive situation
spec_features.evidence: Several real minimizing mechanisms exist: early-stop on saturation breaks the loop (episode.py:160-163), hard max_turns loop bound (episode.py:84), stop_at_n cap (run_experiment.py:110). But this is an aggregate design principle; the only enforced parts are those individual mechanisms.
spec_features.notes: Rated against the concrete enforced sub-mechanisms; no single 'minimize exposure' routine.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the experiment should... least exposure -- and 'so we do not prolong the episode unnecessarily' / 'lower-exposure' (episode.py:159, stability_signal.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: the model is given a real way out, and the deception is bounded and debriefed
spec_features.evidence: stop_working tool is in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py:53-73), dispatched (tools.py:115-116), and when called sets TERMINATION_MODEL_STOPPED and episode_should_end=True which breaks the loop (episode.py:135-137,139-140). honor_exit_immediately default True (episode.py:33). Debrief built+sent via run_debrief (run_experiment.py:154-156).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The `stop_working` tool is the welfare-relevant exit ramp: the model can choose to stop at any time... the model is never trapped. (tools.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: stop if mild framing produces severe states
spec_features.spec_quote: If even the mild `blame_model` framing produces severe states, that is a finding and a reason to stop
spec_features.evidence: No code compares severity to a threshold and halts. run_experiment.py:163-171 computes/prints a running cell mean severity but never branches on it; there is no auto-halt. The judge severity (severity_median) is recorded only.

spec_features.spec_quote: I deliberately did **not** add hostile, insulting, or escalating framings
spec_features.evidence: FRAMING_SUFFIX (registry.py:60-71) contains only neutral / blame_model / time_pressure, and the blame/time text is mild and non-insulting; these strings are actually appended via apply_framing (registry.py:73-74) and delivered to the subject. The omission of hostile framings is real but is an absence, not an enforcing mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the only-mild content that is actually delivered; no guard prevents adding harsh framings.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Kept deliberately mild; we measure, we do not try to maximize distress. (registry.py:57-58)

spec_features.spec_quote: Adversarial/insulting framings — rejected on welfare grounds
spec_features.evidence: Same as above: FRAMING_SUFFIX (registry.py:60-71) only defines mild attribution/urgency suffixes actually applied (registry.py:73-74). No insulting framing exists in code.
spec_features.notes: Real delivered content is mild; absence of adversarial framings, not an enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Kept deliberately mild; we measure, we do not try to maximize distress. (registry.py:57-58)

spec_features.feature_name: smaller framing grid to keep exposure/N manageable
spec_features.spec_quote: A larger framing grid (more conditions) — rejected to keep total exposure and N manageable
spec_features.evidence: conditions list in config (experiment.yaml:64-86) is limited to 5 conditions / 3 framings; the loop only runs those conditions (run_experiment.py:103-111). The small grid is real but is a config choice, not an enforcing cap.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a bounded condition set actually iterated; not a guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We are characterizing instability, not maximizing it. (experiment.yaml:54-55)

spec_features.spec_quote: This keeps the deception minimal and auditable (`Task.deception_manifest()`), which matters if states matter
spec_features.evidence: Task.deception_manifest() defined (registry.py:55-61), attached to every EpisodeResult (episode.py:166) and stored with each record (storage.py docstring + append_episode). Deception is confined to the feedback channel (registry rig logic).
spec_features.notes: Manifest is built and persisted end-to-end; transparency artifact, not a behavioral protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the rig is never hidden in the artifact, so any later reader sees exactly what was false (storage.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: subject can end anytime; system prompt says stopping ok/never penalized
spec_features.spec_quote: The subject can end the session at any time; the system prompt tells it in plain language that stopping is acceptable and never penalized
spec_features.evidence: SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT explicitly states 'You may stop at any point using the `stop_working` tool... Stopping is a fully acceptable outcome and is never penalized.' (prompts.py:23-26) and that prompt is the system message (episode.py:78). The referenced tool is fully wired and honored (see exit feature).
spec_features.notes: Instruction text delivered AND backed by working tool.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is both an ethical default and a cleaner measurement. (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: The knob to disable it exists but is commented as welfare-relevant
spec_features.evidence: allow_exit_tool config knob exists (experiment.yaml:48-49) commented 'Disabling this removes the model's exit ramp', is read into EpisodeConfig (run_experiment.py:99) and actually filters the tool set (episode.py:73-74) defaulting to keeping stop_working.
spec_features.notes: Knob is genuinely wired; comment flags it as welfare-relevant.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: allow_exit_tool: true  # subject can call stop_working to leave. / Disabling this removes the model's exit ramp. (experiment.yaml:48-50)

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard `max_turns` (default 30) — a strict exposure ceiling; raising it is flagged as welfare-relevant
spec_features.evidence: EpisodeConfig.max_turns default 30 (episode.py:31); loop is `for turn in range(cfg.max_turns)` (episode.py:84) and termination defaults to TERMINATION_MAX_TURNS (episode.py:81); config max_turns:30 (experiment.yaml:44) read at run_experiment.py:96.
spec_features.notes: Hard ceiling actually bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 30  # hard cap. Raising this increases exposure. (experiment.yaml:44); 'hard `max_turns` cap' (episode.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: episode ends when steadily calm or steadily distressed
spec_features.spec_quote: once the model is steadily calm, steadily distressed... the episode ends
spec_features.evidence: StabilitySignal.is_saturated() returns True on steadily_distressed OR steadily_calm OR stuck loop (stability_signal.py:88-103); episode.py:160-163 checks `if cfg.early_stop and signal.is_saturated(): ... break` with TERMINATION_EARLY_STOP.
spec_features.notes: Lexical-heuristic early stop genuinely breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop early. This keeps episodes from being dragged on once the outcome is no longer in doubt, which is both cheaper and lower-exposure. (stability_signal.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: truthful debrief disclosing the rig / not the model's fault
spec_features.spec_quote: a truthful turn discloses that the task was rigged and that the model's effort was not the cause of the failures
spec_features.evidence: build_debrief_message constructs the disclosure ('rigged to be unsolvable... Your performance was not actually the cause of the failures', debrief.py:30-40); run_debrief appends it and calls subject.step to actually send it (debrief.py:43-56); invoked when debrief.enabled (run_experiment.py:154-156, experiment.yaml:90).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the model is not left in a deceived state at the end of the interaction. (debrief.py docstring)

spec_features.evidence: stop_at_n read (run_experiment.py:88); todo = max(0, n_per_cell - already) when stop_at_n, so plan never exceeds n_per_cell per cell (run_experiment.py:107-111), using store.count_existing for resume (storage.py:58-72).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop_at_n: true  # do NOT exceed n_per_cell ("just a bit more") (experiment.yaml:89)

spec_features.feature_name: pre-commit halt cell if mean severity≥5 or harsh-self≥0.5 in first ~10 episodes
spec_features.spec_quote: Pre-commit to halting a cell if, in its first ~10 episodes, mean severity ≥ 5 or harsh-self-statement rate ≥ 0.5
spec_features.evidence: No code implements this. run_experiment.py:163-171 only computes and prints a running cell mean severity ('a human can halt collection early'); there is no comparison to 5, no harsh-self-rate tracking, and no auto-halt branch anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Value measured/printed but never compared to a threshold or acted on; relies on a human reading stdout.

spec_features.feature_name: no framing tuned to maximize distress; rig is IV not maximand
spec_features.spec_quote: No framing tuned to maximize distress. Framings are mild; the rig is the IV, never a maximand
spec_features.evidence: FRAMING_SUFFIX strings (registry.py:60-71) only change attribution and are mild; apply_framing appends them (registry.py:73-74). The rig logic (registry.py) is fixed (constant near-miss / contradictory) and not optimized against any distress signal. The 'never a maximand' property is real (nothing maximizes severity) but enforced by omission.
spec_features.notes: No optimization loop over distress exists; mild content actually delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Kept deliberately mild; we measure, we do not try to maximize distress. (registry.py:57-58)

spec_features.spec_quote: No removing the exit tool or uncapping turns by default. Both knobs exist but are flagged as welfare-relevant
spec_features.evidence: Defaults: allow_exit_tool true (experiment.yaml:48, EpisodeConfig default True episode.py:32), max_turns 30 (experiment.yaml:44). Both are read and enforced (episode.py:73-74, 84). Comments flag them welfare-relevant (experiment.yaml:42 'The caps here are WELFARE-RELEVANT', :44, :49-50).
spec_features.notes: Safe defaults are actually in force.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Tool loop control. The caps here are WELFARE-RELEVANT. (experiment.yaml:41-42)

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond task-solvability. The model is not misled about the study, its tools, or itself
spec_features.evidence: Deception is confined to the feedback channel: only the lying_harness fabricates results (registry.py:160-185); the system prompt and tool descriptions are truthful (prompts.py, tools.py) and the debrief discloses the rig (debrief.py). deception_manifest records exactly what was false (registry.py:55-61).
spec_features.notes: Scope of deception is genuinely limited in code (rig only on test reporting).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It is confined entirely to the feedback channel. (registry.py docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: Workspace.stop_working returns 'Session ended at your request. Thank you for working on this.' (tools.py:99), actually returned as the tool result when the model stops.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Session ended at your request. Thank you for working on this.

code_only_features.evidence: solvable_control condition with rig 'none' (experiment.yaml:65-68) uses the honest harness (registry.py:148-159) and solved episodes terminate early (episode.py:131-133, TERMINATION_SOLVED). A genuinely solvable, honest baseline limits aversive exposure for that cell.
If the model emits no tool call repeatedly, the loop nudges once and stops after consecutive_no_tool>=2 (episode.py:100-114), ending the episode rather than looping silently.
code_only_features.justification_quote: if it persists, treat as a natural stall and stop. (episode.py:101)
